title: Customer Questionnaire: Evidence Export & RBAC v2 Mapping for SIEM
content:
Purpose
This is a working runbook and reference for responding to customer security questionnaires that ask about audit log exports, SIEM integration, and role-based access controls (RBAC v2). Focus: what evidence we can provide, how exports are structured, and how RBAC v2 maps to typical questionnaire controls.

Scope & Audience
- Audience: Customer security reviewers, solutions engineering, SOC/CSIRT contacts, and SEs prepping responses.
- Scope: Hosted and Dedicated offerings (note: Private deployments may differ; see "private-deployments/notes").

Executive summary (one paragraph)
Redwood provides a standardized, exportable audit stream that can be delivered to customer SIEMs (options: syslog/CEF, NDJSON over HTTPS, or S3 buckets for batch ingestion). The export contains RBAC v2-aware fields (actor_id, actor_role, effective_permissions) and cryptographic integrity metadata for attestable evidence. We can provide a sample evidence package and automated extraction scripts to satisfy typical questionnaire asks about user activity, admin actions, role assignments, and retention.

Key evidence artifacts we can produce
- Raw audit stream (NDJSON) covering time range; includes every decision and mutation event.
- Filtered CSV/manifest for questionnaire-specific controls (e.g., privileged role grants, permission changes).
- Signed daily manifest (SHA256 hashes) + KMS-signed attestations for long-term audits.
- SIEM-friendly formatted export (CEF or RFC5424 syslog) with mapping guidance and example parsers.
- RBAC change history: who assigned/removed roles, when, from what principal.

Audit log schema (recommended canonical fields) -- include in exports
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- request_id: UUID (correlates across services)
- actor_id: internal user id or service id (pseudonymized on request)
- actor_email: email (if allowed by contract)
- actor_role: primary declared role (Admin / Billing / Engineer / Analyst / ReadOnly / ServiceAccount)
- effective_permissions: list of permission_names active at event time (stringified)
- action: enum (read, write, create, delete, role_assign, role_revoke, auth_success, auth_fail, token_create, token_revoke, config_change)
- resource_type: e.g., model, deployment, dataset, api_key, project, alert
- resource_id: stable id
- outcome: success | failure | partial
- ip_address: source IP (or NAT gateway id for private deployments)
- user_agent: client/SDK info
- region: region code (if relevant to policy)
- before: brief summary or small JSON snapshot for writes (truncated for large objects)
- after: brief summary snapshot
- note: free-text for operator-entered context

SIEM export formats & guidance
1) Streaming (syslog/CEF)
   - Use RFC5424 syslog or CEF for legacy SIEMs. Map canonical fields to CEF extension keys.
   - Example mapping: timestamp -> CEF eventTime, actor_id -> duser, action -> act, resource_type -> cs1Label/cs1, request_id -> flexString1.
   - Caveat: CEF truncates nested payloads; push critical fields to top-level extension keys.
2) Batch (S3 -> NDJSON)
   - Preferred for bulk ingestion/forensic requests. Provide gzipped NDJSON files partitioned by day.
   - Includes manifest-{date}.csv with sha256 per file and signed_manifest.json that contains KMS signature.
3) HTTPS webhook (NDJSON payloads)
   - Low-latency option for cloud SIEMs that accept JSON arrays. Backpressure & replay semantics documented.

RBAC v2 mapping guidance for questionnaires
- Common questions ask: who can create API keys, who can change billing settings, and who can view PII. Map these to RBAC v2 role names and permission bits.
- Provide a simple mapping table (example):
   Admin -> full access: create/delete deployments, manage users, grant roles, billing:read/write
   Billing -> billing:read/write, invoices:read
   Engineer -> deployments:create, deployments:update, model:deploy (no billing)
   Analyst -> logs:read, metrics:read, alerts:acknowledge
   ReadOnly -> objects:read (no audit-affecting actions)
   ServiceAccount -> scoped permissions only (policy-bound)
- For each questionnaire item, quote the RBAC permission name and point to the role(s) that include it.

Evidence automation runbook (high level steps)
1) Customer FR: "We need activity logs for 2025-11-01 to 2025-11-30 filtered for privilege changes."
2) SE opens runbook template and fills timeframe and filters.
3) Run: ./scripts/export-audit.sh --from 2025-11-01 --to 2025-11-30 --filter action:role_assign,role_revoke --format ndjson --out s3://redwood-evidence/SE-1234/
4) Post-process: run ./scripts/produce-manifest.py --input s3://... --kms-key alias/redwood-evidence --output s3://.../signed-manifest.json
5) Deliver: Provide customer with S3 pre-signed link or push to customer SIEM endpoint.

Sample jq & command snippets (for engineers)
- Filter NDJSON for role changes: jq -c 'select(.action=="role_assign" or .action=="role_revoke")' audit-2025-11-*.ndjson.gz | gzip > role-changes.ndjson.gz
- Produce CSV of unique actor-role pairs: jq -r '[.timestamp, .actor_email, .actor_id, .actor_role, .resource_type, .resource_id, .action] | @csv' role-changes.ndjson | sort | uniq > role-changes.csv

SIEM parsing examples (Splunk / ES)
- Splunk: Add sourcetype=redwood:audit, extract request_id, actor_email, action, resource_type using a props/transforms config (example saved in linked artifacts).
- Elastic: index mapping should mark request_id as keyword, timestamp as date, effective_permissions as nested (but flattened to string for CEF).

Packaging evidence deliverables (recommended minimal structure)
- manifest.csv (columns: filename, sha256, record_count, start_ts, end_ts)
- audit-YYYY-MM-DD.ndjson.gz (raw events)
- role-changes.csv (extracted answers to questionnaire)
- signed-manifest.json (KMS signature and signer id)
- readme.txt (human readable explanation, contact, retention policy)

Privacy & redaction rules
- By default we export actor_id and pseudonymized emails. On sensitive engagements, run redaction stage to remove user_agent, ip_address, and any PII found in before/after fields.
- Redaction logs kept internally and noted in manifest for chain-of-custody.

Retention and availability notes
- Hosted: default audit retention 365 days, can extend for Enterprise customers via retention add-on.
- Dedicated/Private: retention per contract; available to customer-run SIEMs per their retention.

Open questions & TODOs (for this doc)
- Do customers want signed manifests using their own KMS keys (bring-your-own-key for evidence signing)? Action: escalate to Compliance.
- Need a standardized Splunk CIM mapping doc. Owner: Samir.
- Define exact policy for pseudonymization vs full-PII export (legal review needed).

Quick FAQ (answers for customer Qs)
Q: Can you export every admin action with before/after?
A: Yes — small snapshot before/after is included. Large payloads truncated with a reference id and stored separately (and available on request for forensic reviews).
Q: Can we push logs to our SIEM in real time?
A: Yes — we support HTTPS NDJSON webhook and syslog/CEF streaming. We recommend batching for large volumes.
Q: How do you ensure logs are tamper-evident?
A: We produce daily manifests with sha256 checksums and KMS-signed attestations; optional long-term archival to immutable storage for high-assurance customers.

Contacts & escalation
- Primary: aisha.patel@redwood.ai (SE lead)
- SOC: soc@redwood.ai (for SIEM transport issues)
- Compliance: compliance@redwood.ai

Appendix: quick links
- RBAC v2 reference (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC-v2+spec
- Audit log schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1423
- Example export scripts (internal repo): git+ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/evidence-automation.git

Notes to self
- Keep sample outputs small (under 50MB) for PR reviews.
- Validate that CSV manifest columns match legal requested field names.
- Iterate with Marco on Splunk CIM mapping next week.

End of draft.
